Have you had times when you felt unusually high, energized, or irritable?
Unusually high or energized? Um, no, I don't think so. Honestly, I kind of wish I had more energy sometimes! Most days I feel like I'm just trying to keep
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Down or depressed? No, I really don't think so. I mean, I know sometimes it can almost look like that from the outside? Like, my mom was actually asking me that the other day because since I haven't been working, I spend a lot of time just... trying to figure out what to do with my day, and I can get really bogged down. But I don't feel sad or hopeless or anything like that. It's not like a dark cloud hanging over me or anything. 

I actually still get really excited about things! Like, I'll get super into a new
Do your emotions tend to shift very quickly in response to things that happen, like going from feeling okay to very upset within a short time?

Shift quickly? Um... no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, obviously if something genuinely upsetting happens I'll get upset, but it's not like a light switch, you know? Going from totally fine to just completely falling apart
Did this start after a specific stressful event or major life change?
A specific stressful event? Um... no, I really don't think so. I mean, it would almost be easier if I could point to something like that, you know
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

Worrying? Um... no, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I worry without a clear reason. Obviously, I worry about normal, actual things. Like, since I'm not working right now, I definitely have moments where I
Do you often feel tense or unable to relax?

Tense or unable to relax? Um... no, I wouldn't say that's a big issue for me. I mean, I definitely have moments where I'm wound up, especially if I'm trying to get something done and I keep getting sidetracked, which happens a lot, obviously. But just sitting there feeling physically tense for no reason? No, not really. If anything, I'm usually just trying to find something to do, you know? Like, I'll sit down to watch TV and I'll end up on my phone, or I'll get up to get a snack and then I'll start reorganizing the pantry because I noticed the cans were out of order. So I guess you could say I'm always kind of in motion, but it's not because I feel stressed or tight in my muscles. It's more just... I can't just sit and do nothing. But actual tension? Like clenching my jaw or my shoulders being up by my ears? No, I don't really get that unless there's a specific reason, like an argument or a deadline I forgot about. Otherwise, I'm pretty loose, just... busy, I guess you'd call it.
Did you have these kinds of trouble with focus or sitting still when you were a child?
Oh, absolutely. I mean, when I really sit down and think about it... looking back, this was already a huge part of me all the way back in elementary school. I was always that one
When you were a child, did these attention or activity problems cause trouble in more than one place, like both at school and at home?

Trouble in more than one place? Um... well, I'm not really sure if I can say it caused *trouble* everywhere. I mean, school was definitely its own thing, right? Like, you have to sit at a desk, and you're supposed to just listen to the teacher talk about fractions or the Oregon Trail or whatever for what feels like hours. And that was just... impossible for me. I was always getting my name on the board or losing recess because I was talking to my friends or drawing on my desk or just generally not doing what I was supposed to be doing. So that was definitely a thing. 

But at home? I don't know if I'd call it trouble. My mom was always telling me to settle down or to go play outside because I was running laps around the living room, but I don't remember it being a huge problem, you know? Like, I wasn't getting grounded for it or anything. It was just more like, "Oh, there she goes again, she just has a lot of energy." I remember I had this one phase where I would try to build these elaborate forts out of all the sofa cushions and blankets, and I'd just leave them up for days, and my parents would get so annoyed because they couldn't sit down to watch the news. But I wouldn't say it was like... *trouble*. Just me being me, I guess? I mean, I definitely drove my older sister crazy because I was always in her room touching her stuff and asking a million questions when she was trying to do her homework, but siblings just do that, right? So, yeah, I'm not really sure if it was a problem in both places. School, for sure. Home... maybe just a little annoying to other people?
As a child, did your difficulty sitting still or staying focused ever get you into trouble at home?

Well, like I was just saying... I don't know if "trouble" is the right word for it. I mean, my parents never really sat me down and gave me major punishments or anything like that. It was more just... constant friction, I guess? Like, I remember this one time—I must have been about eight or nine—and my mom had just finished cleaning the whole house because my grandparents were coming over for Sunday dinner. And I was supposed to be in my room, cleaning up my toys, which was always a disaster zone anyway. But instead of cleaning, I found this old box of beads and string I'd gotten for my birthday months ago, and I decided right then and there I was going to make a necklace for my grandma. 

So I brought the beads out into the hallway, and of course, I spilled the entire container. Thousands of these tiny, little plastic beads just everywhere, all over the hardwood floor. And I was crawling around trying to pick them up, but I kept getting distracted by the different colors, sorting them instead of actually putting them away. My mom came up the stairs and just about lost her mind. She was yelling about how I never listen and how I can't stay on task for five minutes. But even then, she didn't ground me. She just made me vacuum them all up, which was devastating because I wanted to make that necklace. 

So, did I get into trouble? I mean, they were definitely exasperated with me a lot. My dad used to call me his "little tornado" because I'd just blow through a room, leave a mess, and be onto the next thing before anyone even realized what happened. But they didn't really treat it like I was being bad, you know? Just... exhausting. So I wouldn't say I was in major trouble at home, just... constantly being told to slow down or pay attention to what I was doing.
As a child, did your teachers ever complain that you were easily distracted?

Oh, easily distracted? Um... well, actually, I don't really remember them saying that specifically. I mean, they definitely complained about me talking too much, or not staying in my seat, like I mentioned before. But distracted? I'm not sure. I feel like I was always paying attention to *something*, just maybe not the thing they wanted me to pay attention to. Like, I remember in fourth grade, Mr. Henderson's class, I was absolutely fascinated by this spider that had built a web right outside the window next to my desk. I would watch it for what felt like hours, trying to see if it would catch a fly. And he would get so annoyed because I wasn't looking at the chalkboard. But I wasn't distracted, I was completely focused on the spider! 

So, I don't know if they used that word. They probably just thought I was being defiant or something. I mean, I do remember my report cards always saying things like "needs to apply herself" or "has potential but lacks discipline." But I don't recall any specific complaints about being easily distracted. It was more about the talking and the fidgeting and the not finishing my worksheets because I was too busy drawing elaborate doodles in the margins. I had this whole series of doodles about these little alien creatures that lived in a volcano... anyway, yeah, I don't think they specifically complained about me being distracted. Just... difficult, maybe?
Do you often have trouble finishing tasks because your attention drifts?
Oh, finishing tasks... yes. Yes, absolutely. It's actually a huge point of contention between me and my husband right now. Because he'll ask me to handle just a few things in a specific
As a child, were you often in trouble at home because you couldn’t stay focused or sit still?

Wait, didn't we... I feel like we just talked about this, didn't we? About being in trouble at home? Because I remember saying that I wouldn't really call it "trouble" in the traditional sense, you know? Like, I wasn't getting grounded for a week or having my television privileges taken away. It was more like... exasperation. Like my dad calling me his "little tornado" because I was always moving and leaving a trail of destruction behind me. 

But I mean, if you're asking if my parents were frustrated with me, then yes, absolutely. It was just a constant stream of "slow down," "pay attention," "look at what you're doing." Like that time with the beads I was telling you about, right before the grandparents came over. My mom was so upset, not because I was being malicious, but because I just couldn't stick to the simple task of cleaning my room. I got completely sidetracked by wanting to make a necklace. And that was the story of my childhood, really. Starting one thing, getting distracted by something else, and leaving a mess in the middle. So I guess I wasn't in "trouble" like a bad kid, but I was definitely a handful. They were always having to redirect me or remind me to finish what I started. It's funny, because my husband does the exact same thing now... but yeah, I think we already covered the childhood stuff, right?
As a child, did these same problems ever get you in trouble with friends or during activities outside of school?

Trouble with friends? Um... no, not really. I mean, I don't remember getting into actual trouble during activities or with other kids. I was definitely energetic, you know, always wanting to run around or start a new game. Like, if we were playing tag, I'd get bored of being "it" and suddenly decide we were playing hide-and-seek instead, and I'd just go hide without telling anyone. And then they'd be wandering around the neighborhood looking for me while I was up in the neighbor's apple tree, completely absorbed in trying to get the highest apple I could reach. 

So maybe they got a little annoyed sometimes because I wouldn't stick to the rules of whatever we were doing, but it wasn't like I was losing friends over it. I was just the one who was always bouncing off the walls. In Girl Scouts, I remember we had this project where we were supposed to be making birdhouses, and I spent the whole time painting the little wooden pieces instead of actually assembling them. The troop leader, Mrs. Gable—she had this very specific way she wanted things done—she just sighed and ended up putting mine together for me because I was so focused on making the roof look like a rainbow. But it wasn't really "trouble," just... me being me, I guess. I always had friends, we just kind of rolled with it. I don't think it was a big issue outside of school or home.
As a child, did these problems ever cause real trouble for you in activities outside of school, like sports, clubs, or with friends?
I know we just touched on friends and Girl Scouts, and I said it wasn't really "trouble" in that sense... but, you know, when you say "real trouble," my mind
As a child, did these problems ever cause real trouble for you in activities outside of school, like sports, clubs, or with friends?

...my mind goes straight to soccer. Oh, my goodness, soccer. I played for maybe three seasons when I was around eight or nine? And I think that's where the distraction really became a problem, like an actual issue for the team. Because you're supposed to be watching the ball, right? You're supposed to stay in your position. But I played goalie for a few games, which was just a terrible idea in hindsight, because there's so much downtime. I remember this one specific game, it was a Saturday morning, the grass was still kind of wet with dew, and I found this incredible patch of clovers right by the goalpost. I was convinced I was going to find a four-leaf clover. I was literally on my hands and knees, sifting through the grass, completely oblivious. And the other team came down the field and scored. Just kicked it right past me while I was looking at weeds. My coach, Mr. Henderson, he was this really intense guy who took nine-year-old soccer way too seriously, he had to stop the game and yell across the field, "Get up! Pay attention to the game!" It was so embarrassing, and the other kids were definitely mad at me for losing the point. 

And then there was piano lessons. My parents really wanted me to play piano, so I had this lovely older lady, Mrs. Higgins, who taught out of her living room. But I couldn't sit on the bench for the whole thirty minutes. I'd play a scale, and then I'd see her cat walk by, and I just had to go pet the cat. Or I'd start looking at the metronome and taking it apart in my head, trying to figure out how the little weight made it tick faster or slower. She actually ended up telling my mom that she didn't think I was "ready" for formal instruction because I wouldn't sit still and focus on the sheet music. So I guess I got kicked out of piano? If you can call it that. So, yeah, I didn't lose friends over it, but it definitely caused some friction and, you know, got me benched in soccer and politely dismissed from piano. It was always just... I couldn't stay locked in on what I was supposed to be doing if something else caught my eye. Which, now that I think about it, is probably why I struggle so much with sitting through long meetings now, but back then it was clovers and cats.

But I mean, if you're asking if my parents were frustrated with me, then yes, absolutely. It was just a constant stream of "slow down," "pay attention," "look at what you're doing." Like that time with the beads I was telling you about, right before the grandparents came over. My mom was so upset, not because I was being malicious, but because I just couldn't stick to the simple task of cleaning my room. I got completely sidetracked by wanting to make a necklace. And that was the story of my childhood, really. Starting one thing, getting distracted by something else, and leaving a mess in the middle. So I guess I wasn't in "trouble" like a bad kid, but I was definitely a handful. They were always having to redirect me or remind me to finish what I started. Trouble with friends? Um... no, not really. I mean, I don't remember getting into actual trouble during activities or with other kids. I was definitely energetic, you know, always wanting to run around or start a new game. Like, if we were playing tag, I'd get bored of being "it" and suddenly decide we were playing hide-and-seek instead, and I'd just go hide without telling anyone. And then they'd be wandering around the neighborhood looking for me while I was up in the neighbor's apple tree, completely absorbed in trying to get the highest apple I could reach. 

So maybe they got a little annoyed sometimes because I wouldn't stick to the rules of whatever we were doing, but it wasn't like I was losing friends over it. I was just the one who was always bouncing off the walls. In Girl Scouts, I remember we had this project where we were supposed to be making birdhouses, and I spent the whole time painting the little wooden pieces instead of actually assembling them. The troop leader, Mrs. Gable—she had this very specific way she wanted things done—she just sighed and ended up putting mine together for me because I was so focused on making the roof look like a rainbow. But it wasn't really "trouble," just... me being me, I guess. I always had friends, we just kind of rolled with it. I don't think it was a big issue outside of school or home.

doctor.question: As a child, did these problems ever cause real trouble for you in activities outside of school, like sports, clubs, or with friends?

patient.answer:
...my mind goes straight to soccer. Oh, my goodness, soccer. I played for maybe three seasons when I was around eight or nine? And I think that's where the distraction really became a problem, like an actual issue for the team. Because you're supposed to be watching the ball, right? You're supposed to stay in your position. But I played goalie for a few games, which was just a terrible idea in hindsight, because there's so much downtime. I remember this one specific game, it was a Saturday morning, the grass was still kind of wet with dew, and I found this incredible patch of clovers right by the goalpost. I was convinced I was going to find a four-leaf clover. I was literally on my hands and knees, sifting through the grass, completely oblivious. And the other team came down the field and scored. Just kicked it right past me while I was looking at weeds. My coach, Mr. Henderson, he was this really intense guy who took nine-year-old soccer way too seriously, he had to stop the game and yell across the field, "Get up! Pay attention to the game!" It was so embarrassing, and the other kids were definitely mad at me for losing the point. 

And then there was piano lessons. My parents really wanted me to play piano, so I had this lovely older lady, Mrs. Higgins, who taught out of her living room. But I couldn't sit on the bench for the whole thirty minutes. I'd play a scale, and then I'd see her cat walk by, and I just had to go pet the cat. Or I'd start looking at the metronome and taking it apart in my head, trying to figure out how the little weight made it tick faster or slower. She actually ended up telling my mom that she didn't think I was "ready" for formal instruction because I wouldn't sit still and focus on the sheet music. So I guess I got kicked out of piano? If you can call it that. So, yeah, I didn't lose friends over it, but it definitely caused some friction and, you know, got me benched in soccer and politely dismissed from piano. It was always just... I couldn't stay locked in on what I was supposed to be doing if something else caught my eye. Which, now that I think about it, is probably why I struggle so much with sitting through long meetings now, but back then it was clovers and cats.
